title: The Secret Teachings of All Ages
author: Manly P. Hall
description: The Secret Teachings of All Ages: An Encyclopedic Outline of Masonic, Hermetic, Qabbalistic and Rosicrucian Symbolical Philosophy by Manly P. Hall (San Francisco: H. S. Crocker, 1928), with colour plates by J. Augustus Knapp. Written when Hall was in his twenties and published by subscription in a grand folio edition, it is the most famous encyclopedia of Western esotericism. Its forty-six chapters survey the ancient mysteries and secret societies, Atlantis and the gods of antiquity, the life and philosophy of Pythagoras and Pythagorean mathematics, the Hermetic and Isiac traditions, the Kabbalah and the Tree of Life, Tarot, alchemy and its theory, the Rosicrucians and Freemasons, Bacon, Shakespeare and the cipher controversies, sacred birds, flowers and stones, astrology and the zodiac, Christian mysticism and American destiny. Despite uneven scholarship, it shaped twentieth-century occultism and remains a standard reference on esoteric symbolism.
